//PROCESS: Using arrays of objects

<New code>

//PROCESS: loop through each element of an array of objects 
var loopThroughArrayOfObjects = function ( exampleArr ) {
	for ( i in exampleArr ) {			// loop through each object of the array
	
		// do something with exampleArr[ i ].oneProperty
		// do something with exampleArr[ i ].anotherProperty
		// do something with exampleArr[ i ].yetAnotherProperty
	}
}

Using arrays of objects to create a table

Arrays of objects are used to contain a series of multiples of objects. This is perhaps the most common complex data structure.

For example, let's create a table of information about the best land speed records. We can do this with the following procedure:

  1. Declare and initialize the chart data as an array of objects.
  2. Open the <table> and create the <thead> code.
  3. Loop through each element of the array.
    1. Each element of the array is an object, and it has object properties that you can access.
    2. Open a new <tr>.
    3. Add a series of <td>s, that add the object data inside.
    4. Close the </td>.
  4. Close the </table> and output it.

...is made with the following code:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
    <head>
        <meta charset="UTF-8">
        <title>PROCESS: Using arrays of objects to create a table</title>
        <meta name="description" content="Learn how to use arrays of objects to create a table">
        <meta name="author" content="Dave Drapak">
        <script>
            //INIT: declare the array of objects
            //      data taken from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_vehicle_speed_records
            var speedRecordArr = [
                { category: 'Land speed record', speed: 1228, vehicle: 'ThrustSSC', operator: 'Andy Green', date: '15 October, 1997' },
                { category: 'Wheel-driven', speed: 775.106, vehicle: 'Vesco Turbinator', operator: 'Don Vesco', date: '18 October, 2001' },
                { category: 'Motorcycle', speed: 605.697, vehicle: 'Ack Attack', operator: 'Rocky Robinson', date: '25 September, 2010' },
                { category: 'Diesel-powered', speed: 563.995, vehicle: 'JCB DieselMax', operator: 'Andy Green', date: '23 August, 2006' },
                { category: 'Electric-powered', speed: 495.14, vehicle: 'Buckeye Bullet 2.5', operator: 'Roger Schroer', date: '24 August, 2010' },
                { category: 'Steam-powered', speed: 225.06, vehicle: 'Inspiration', operator: 'Charles Burnett III', date: '25 August, 2009' },
                { category: 'Wind-powered', speed: 203.09, vehicle: 'Ecotricity Greenbird', operator: 'Richard Jenkins', date: '26 March, 2009' },
                { category: 'Human-powered bicycle', speed: 133.78, vehicle: 'VeloX3', operator: 'Sebastiaan Bowier', date: '14 September, 2013' },
                { category: 'Paced bicycle', speed: 268.831, vehicle: 'custom made', operator: 'Fred Rompelberg', date: '15 October, 1995' },
                { category: 'Solar-powered', speed: 88.8, vehicle: 'Sunswift IV "IVy"', operator: 'Barton Mawer', date: '7 January, 2011' },
                { category: 'Radio-controlled car', speed: 325.12, vehicle: 'RC Bullet', operator: 'Nic Case', date: '25 October, 2014' },
                { category: 'Tracked vehicle', speed: 82.23, vehicle: 'FV101 Scorpion reconnaissance vehicle', operator: '', date: '26 March, 2002' },
                { category: 'On ice', speed: 331.61, vehicle: 'Audi RS6', operator: 'Janne Laitinen', date: '6 March, 2011' },
                { category: 'Lunar rover', speed: 17, vehicle: 'Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-003)', operator: 'Eugene Cernan', date: '31 July, 1972' }
            ];
            
            var mainProcedure = function () {
                console.log('in mainProcedure...');
                
                var tableCode       = createTable( speedRecordArr );
                outputTable( tableCode );
            }
            
            //PROCESS:  create a table of speed record information based on the information 
            //          stored inside an array of records
            var createTable = function ( speedRecordArr ) {
                // create a variable to hold the table's code, and add the beginning of the table
                var tableHTML 
                    = "<table>"     
                        + "<thead><tr>"
                            + "<th>Category</th>" 
                            + "<th>Speed (km/h)</th>" 
                            + "<th>Vehicle</th>" 
                            + "<th>Operator</th>"
                            + "<th>Date</th>" 
                        + "</tr></thead><tbody>"
                
                // loop through each element of speedRecordArr and create a table row for object contained inside
                for ( i in speedRecordArr ) {
                    console.log( 'in createTable..., i=' + i + ", speedRecordArr[ i ]=" + speedRecordArr[ i ] );
                    
                    tableHTML = tableHTML 
                        + "<tr>" // open a new row
                            + "<td>" + speedRecordArr[ i ].category + "</td>"
                            + "<td>" + speedRecordArr[ i ].speed + "</td>"
                            + "<td>" + speedRecordArr[ i ].vehicle + "</td>"
                            + "<td>" + speedRecordArr[ i ].operator + "</td>"
                            + "<td>" + speedRecordArr[ i ].date + "</td>"
                        + "</tr>"; // close the row
                }
                
                // finish by adding the end of the table code
                tableHTML = tableHTML 
                    + "</tbody></table>";
                    
                return tableHTML;
            }
            
            //OUTPUT: display the screen information in an alert
            var outputTable = function ( tableCode ) {
                console.log('in outputTable...');
                document.getElementById('outputID').innerHTML = tableCode;
            }
        </script>
    </head>
    <body>
        <p>
            <button onclick="mainProcedure();">Click to generate the table</button>
        </p>
        <div id="outputID"></div>
    </body>
</html>

            ];
                        
            var mainProcedureMap = function () {
                console.log('in mainProcedure...');

                var mapCode = createMapCode( parkingMeterArr );
                outputMap( mapCode );
            }
            
            //INPUT: get the screen height and width (as a number of pixels), and return the info as an object
            var getScreenInformation = function () {
                return {
                    width:      window.innerWidth,
                    height:     window.innerHeight
                };
            }
            
            //PROCESS:  create a map of parking meters based on the array of objects, parkingMeterArr
            var createMapCode = function ( parkingMeterArr ) {
                // get the screen properties
                var screenObj = getScreenInformation();
                
                // get the minimum and maximum values of all the parts of the array of objects
                var dataBoundariesObj = getMinsAndMaxs( parkingMeterArr );
                                
                // create a variable to hold the map's code 
                var mapHTML = "";
                
                // loop through each element of speedRecordArr and create a table row for object contained inside
                for ( i in parkingMeterArr ) {
                    //console.log( 'in createMapCode..., i=' + i + ", parkingMeterArr[ i ]=" + parkingMeterArr[ i ] );

                    var positionCode = calculatePositionCode( 
                        {
                            elementX:           parkingMeterArr[ i ].longitude,
                            elementY:           parkingMeterArr[ i ].latitude,
                            
                            xMin:               dataBoundariesObj.longitudeMin,
                            xMax:               dataBoundariesObj.longitudeMax,
                            yMin:               dataBoundariesObj.latitudeMin,
                            yMax:               dataBoundariesObj.latitudeMax,
                            screenWidth:        screenObj.width,
                            screenHeight:       screenObj.height
                        }
                    );

                    mapHTML = mapHTML 
                        + "<div class='duration"
                        + parkingMeterArr[ i ].meterDuration
                        + "class' style='"
                        + positionCode
                        + "' title='latitude: "
                        + parkingMeterArr[ i ].latitude
                        + ", longitude: "
                        + parkingMeterArr[ i ].longitude
                        + ", meter duration: "
                        + parkingMeterArr[ i ].meterDuration
                        + "'></div>";
                }
                return mapHTML;
            }
            
            //PROCESS:  calculate the minimum and maximum values of each property in the array of objects
            //          this assumes that each object is identical in structure and numeric
            //          this outputs the property names with either "Max" or "Max" added to the end
            var getMinsAndMaxs = function ( objArr ) {
                console.log( 'in getMinsAndMaxs...' );
                
                var minsAndMax = {};
                // set up the initial information for comparison using objArr[ 0 ]
                for ( property in objArr [ 0 ] ) {
                    minsAndMax[ property + "Min" ] = objArr[ 0 ][ property ];
                    minsAndMax[ property + "Max" ] = objArr[ 0 ][ property ];
                }
                
                // loop through each element of the array to find the min and max
                for ( i in objArr ) {
                    for ( property in objArr [ i ] ) {
                        minsAndMax[ property + "Min" ] = Math.min( minsAndMax[ property + "Min" ], objArr[ i ][ property ] );
                        minsAndMax[ property + "Max" ] = Math.max( minsAndMax[ property + "Max" ], objArr[ i ][ property ] );
                    }
                }
                
                console.log( minsAndMax );
                return minsAndMax;
            }
            
            //PROCESS:  calculate the positions given x and y coordinates, min/max, and screen information
            //          posObj = { xMin:, xMax:, elementX:, yMin:, yMax:, elementY:, screenWidth:, screenHeight: }
            var calculatePositionCode = function ( posObj ) {
                console.log( 'in calculatePositionCode...' );
                // calculate the data range for both the top and left measures
                var topRange    = posObj.yMax - posObj.yMin;
                var leftRange   = posObj.xMax - posObj.xMin;
                
                // calculate a range and screen dimension so the plotting is as large as possible on the screen
                var range, screenDimension;
                var topRangePerPixel = topRange / posObj.screenHeight;
                var leftRangePerPixel = leftRange / posObj.screenWidth;
                
                if ( topRangePerPixel > leftRangePerPixel ) {
                    range               = topRange; 
                    screenDimension     = posObj.screenHeight;
                } else {
                    range               = leftRange;
                    screenDimension     = posObj.screenWidth;
                }
                
                // calculate the ratio of the coodinates across the screen
                var topDelta    = posObj.yMax - posObj.elementY;
                var leftDelta   = posObj.xMax - posObj.elementX; 
                var topRatio    = ( ( topDelta ) / range );
                var leftRatio   = 1 - ( ( leftDelta ) / range );

                // calculate the final position on the screen
                var topPosition = Math.round( topRatio * screenDimension );
                var leftPosition = Math.round( leftRatio * screenDimension );
                
                return "top: " + topPosition + "px; left: " + leftPosition + "px;" 
            }

            
            //OUTPUT: display the map inside the div #output2ID
            var outputMap = function ( mapCode ) {
                console.log('in outputMap...');
                document.body.style.backgroundColor = "black";
                document.body.innerHTML = mapCode;
            }
        </script>
